correctness.rationale: A point of Hom(K_S,K_T) is a family of source-indexed probability vectors on T with nonempty pairwise disjoint supports. G-invariance identifies weights along each target orbit O, which, when active, determines exactly one G-equivariant map O→S. Such maps biject with S^{G_t}, for t∈O. Transitivity of S forces every source vertex to receive |O|/|S| colors for each chosen orbit, so its common normalization yields barycentric weights of a join of discrete sets of sizes a_O=|S^{G_t}|. The inverse simplex maps are continuous and affine on cells; empty, singleton, and wedge cases follow integrally from joins. Verified independent S3 target orbit sizes (3,6) and option counts (1,3), and noncyclic S4 two 12-element orbits each with two choices, giving a circle. Source proof handles all finite G, not inferred from checks.

value.rationale: A uniform PL homeomorphism for every finite transitive source action is a structural classification beyond Euler traces. Stabilizers determine join factors, yielding exact integral wedge ranks, contractible and empty cases; a noncyclic S4 action with two ordered-pair target orbits yields a fixed circle. This is a naturally motivated symmetry topology result rather than a change of notation for ordinary Hom homology.
